# Temple Scroll Column 67 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 67 | **Condition:** fragmentary (final column)

---

**67:1** Blessed shall you be in the city, and blessed shall you be in the field.

**67:2** Blessed shall be the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground and the fruit of your livestock, the increase of your cattle and the young of your flock.

**67:3** Blessed shall be your basket and your kneading bowl.

**67:4** Blessed shall you be when you come in, and blessed shall you be when you go out.

**67:5** The LORD shall cause your enemies who rise against you to be struck down before you; by one way they shall come out against you, and by seven ways they shall flee before you.

**67:6** But it shall be, if you do not obey the voice of the LORD your God, to keep and to do all his commandments and his statutes [...] all these curses shall come upon you and overtake you.

**67:7** Cursed shall you be in the city, and cursed shall you be in the field.

**67:8** Cursed shall be your basket and your kneading bowl.

**67:9** Cursed shall be the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground, the increase of your cattle and the young of your flock. [...]

**67:10** [...] The LORD shall send upon you the curse, the confusion, and the rebuke in all the sending forth of your hand that you do, until you are destroyed and until you perish quickly, on account of the evil of your deeds, because you have forsaken me.

**67:11** [...] The LORD shall make the pestilence cling to you until he has consumed you from upon the land that you are entering to possess it. [...]

**67:12** [...] because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy and with gladness of heart, when there was abundance of all things. [...]

**67:13** [...] and you shall serve your enemies whom the LORD shall send against you, in hunger and in thirst and in nakedness and in want of all things, and he shall put a yoke of iron upon your neck until he has destroyed you. [...]

**67:14** [...] And all these curses shall come upon you and pursue you and overtake you until you are destroyed, because you did not obey the voice of the LORD your God to keep his commandments and his statutes that he commanded you. [...]

---

*EMET notes: Column 67 is the final column of the Temple Scroll and the most damaged. It draws on Deut 28:3–7 (blessings) and 28:15–48 (curses). The blessing-curse structure mirrors the Deuteronomic covenant formulary. "Because you have forsaken me" — first-person divine voice even in the curse section. "The sending forth of your hand" for משלח ידך preserves the Hebrew idiom. [...] marks genuine lacunae throughout this heavily damaged column. The scroll likely continued with more curse material but the final lines are lost.*
